t: You're looking at Flamsteed House, in the Royal Borough of Greenwich. It takes its name from John Flamsteed, the first Astronomer Royal. He prepared a catalogue of three thousand stars and a star atlas, both published after his death. He made the first recorded observations of Uranus, though he mistakenly logged it as a star. He also laid the foundation stone for the Royal Greenwich Observatory, so this is a good place to think about how closely his name is tied to astronomy in Greenwich.
